question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout once the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The code path is focused and privacy-protective, but disabling existing opt-ins and adding credentialed Data Safety release automation are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh conflicts against current main, and land the PR.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request different disclosure wording, placement, consent-version persistence, or release-lane behavior before repeating emulator and release-lane proof.

options.title: Hold for Play materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until Data Safety CSV, Play Console state, privacy-policy text, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh conflicts against current main, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the clearest prior ownership of the Android release lane and authored the Data Safety automation surface that needs release-policy acceptance.
